DialectModel.description:
How a file is written, so it can be read: the dialect of the W3C's CSV on the Web metadata vocabulary
([Metadata Vocabulary for Tabular Data, section 5.9](https://www.w3.org/TR/tabular-metadata/#dialect-descriptions)),
with its names and defaults, and whyqd's own: `encodingStep`, `rowsPerRecord`, `sheet`, and, for a PDF, `cells`,
`pages`, and `columns`.

One default differs: CSV on the Web trims each cell, and whyqd keeps it as written (`trim` false). A blank line is
a row (`skipBlankRows` false), in both.

encoding.description: The file's encoding, as the WHATWG Encoding Standard names it.
encoding.title: Encoding

quoteChar.description: The character quoting a cell; `null` for none.
quoteChar.title: Quotechar

doubleQuote.description: A quote inside a quoted cell is doubled; if false, escaped by `\`.
doubleQuote.title: Doublequote

skipRows.description: Rows before the header, or before the data where there is no header.
skipRows.title: Skiprows

headerRowCount.description: Header rows; `0` where the file has none.
headerRowCount.title: Headerrowcount

skipBlankRows.description: Leave out blank rows. By default a blank row is a row.
skipBlankRows.title: Skipblankrows

rowsPerRecord.description: The fields in each row of one record, header included, where a record spans several rows: `[47, 1]` is 47 fields on the first row and 1 on the next. Absent where a record is one row.
rowsPerRecord.title: Rowsperrecord

sheet.description: The spreadsheet's sheet, where the file has several.
sheet.title: Sheet

cells.description: How a PDF's cells are found: by its ruling (`lines`), or by where its text sits (`text`). Read from the file where undeclared: `lines` where its ruling gives a table, else `text`.
cells.title: Cells

pages.description: A PDF's pages holding the table, counted from 1: `5-7`, or `1,3,5-7`. Absent for every page.
pages.title: Pages

columns.description: The left edge of each of a PDF table's columns, in points from the page's left, where its cells are found by `text` and the words do not show the columns.
columns.title: Columns

DialectModel.title: DialectModel

ExtensionModel.description:
An action or type a definition uses that whyqd does not include, from the package that provides it.

An extension is known by its package and its name together, since one name in two packages need not do the same
thing. Its version is a range in the Python packaging standard's
[version specifier](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/version-specifiers/) syntax, such as
`>=1.2.3,<2`; a transform records the exact version it ran, as `==1.2.3`.

name.description: The action's or type's name, as a definition writes it.
name.title: Name

kind.description: Whether it is an action or a type.

distribution.description: The installed package that provides it.
distribution.title: Distribution

version.description: The versions of that package the definition accepts.
version.title: Version

iri.description: An IRI giving the extension's meaning.
iri.title: Iri

ExtensionModel.title: ExtensionModel

A field without a policy is read as text.

ReasonModel.description:
Why a crosswalk step holds, in the terms of an SSSOM mapping's justification
([SSSOM data model](https://github.com/mapping-commons/sssom/blob/9287d104437ad702fa4e74b1ea2b42a879b877ae/src/docs/spec-model.md)).
It covers every mapping in its step.

The justification is a term from the
[Semantic Mapping Vocabulary](https://mapping-commons.github.io/semantic-mapping-vocabulary/), recording whether a
person or a tool made the judgement: `semapv:ManualMappingCuration` for a wrangler's own, `semapv:MappingReview`
for a check of someone else's.

author.description: Who made the mapping, by name or identifier.
author.title: Author

confidence.description: How sure the author is, from 0 to 1.
confidence.title: Confidence

seeAlso.description: Where more can be read, by URI.
seeAlso.title: Seealso

reference.description: The versioned source the mapping relies on.

ReasonModel.title: ReasonModel

ReferenceModel.description:
A versioned source a definition relies on: a term list, a correspondence, or what a reason cites.

The pair is SSSOM's source and source version (`subject_source`, `subject_source_version`, in the
[SSSOM data model](https://github.com/mapping-commons/sssom/blob/9287d104437ad702fa4e74b1ea2b42a879b877ae/src/docs/spec-model.md)).
The version is required, since a
definition pins what it relies on and never follows a list's current version.

source.description: The source's IRI, or its path where it is private.
source.title: Source
